area.hero.h1: Heating and cooling repair in Pilsen, Chicago
area.hero.lede: Boilers and radiators, furnaces, central air and ductless systems, for Pilsen brick two-flats, cottages, shops with flats above and the kitchens on 18th Street. Family-owned since 1952, with the owner, Rob, still on the calls.
area.form.title: Book HVAC service in Pilsen
area.services.heading: Every heating and cooling service we offer in Pilsen
area.who.copy: City & Suburban is run from 1225 N Cleaver St, about three miles north of Pilsen, a straight run down Ashland Avenue. Rob, the owner, still runs the calls and does the diagnosis on the jobs that need it.
area.reviews.1.quote: Great company. I called on a Sunday night because my furnace wasn’t working. The repair person was here first thing on Monday morning. Absolutely fantastic. He was friendly and knowledgeable and got my furnace running very quickly. He then reviewed various options with me for the future. It was very easy to send my payment via Zelle. Could not have gone better.
area.reviews.2.quote: Three times, my experience with Suburban Heating and Cooling has exceeded my expectations. The first time I found them as a quick search, my heat went out on a Saturday morning. He was here at 9am that day to fix it. Kind, prompt, and knowledgeable. He explained what he was doing, what he thought about my old furnace, and we agreed to keep fixing it.
area.reviews.3.quote: City and suburban came recommended to me when my furnace kept going out several years ago. My landlord was sending his guy to fix this chronic issue where it kept going out, they'd fix it, it'd go out again. It was a very cold winter for me. Rob responded quickly to my message and set up an appointment. He came, identified the problem, double-checked his work and was back with…
area.reviews.4.quote: Very quick response and was clear on the issue and solution! Rob came out to our place to assess the issue on our furnace and fixed it within a same day! He was transparent on the status of the furnace and provided the solution of the issue im having right away. Definitely found a local business who I can rely on that will come back for sure!
area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a two-flat, a cottage and a storefront
area.scope.1.why: Many Pilsen houses sit below the raised street, so the boiler or furnace is in a low basement and access sets the time.
area.scope.2.why: Pilsen's 19th-century brick two-flats often still heat with a boiler and radiators, a different job from a furnace repair.
area.scope.3.why: In Pilsen's oldest flats the first job can be finding the part, or telling you straight when there isn't one.
area.scope.4.why: Pilsen's boiler-heated flats have no ducts for central air, so cooling usually means ductless mini-splits.
area.scope.5.why: Bakeries and restaurants run rooftop units and kitchen make-up air, so visits are booked around opening hours.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.buildings.heading: What heats and cools your Pilsen building
area.buildings.1.title: Brick two-flat
area.buildings.1.body: A shared boiler and radiators, or a furnace per flat. Condensers on the garage or in the gangway.
area.buildings.2.title: Brick or frame cottage
area.buildings.2.body: Often below the street, with the furnace or boiler in a low basement. Duct runs are short and tight.
area.buildings.3.title: Shop with flats above
area.buildings.3.body: A rooftop unit or split for the store downstairs and a furnace or boiler for the flats.
area.buildings.4.title: Restaurant or bakery
area.buildings.4.body: Rooftop units, kitchen exhaust and make-up air on 18th Street, worked around opening hours.

area.faq.heading: Pilsen HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Is the old boiler in my Pilsen two-flat worth repairing?
area.faq.1.a: Often it is. We diagnose first, and where the boiler has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.faq.2.q: How far is your shop from Pilsen?
area.faq.3.q: Can you work on a furnace in a below-street basement?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC repair in Chicago need a permit?
area.cta.body: Have the make of your boiler, furnace or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. In a below-street basement, mention how we get down to it.

extras.districts.4.hvac: HVAC here: furnaces in frame houses, boilers in the brick two-flats.
extras.faq.2.a: About three miles. The shop is at 1225 N Cleaver St in West Town, and Ashland Avenue runs from there straight into Pilsen. Rob runs the calls himself.
extras.faq.3.a: Yes. Tell us when you call that the basement sits below the street, so we know about low ceilings and tight stairs before we arrive.
extras.faq.4.a: No. Chicago doesn't require a permit to repair, diagnose or maintain heating and cooling. Permits cover installs and construction, so a company's permit count says little about its repair work.
extras.faq.5.a: Monday to Friday, 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM, and Saturday, 6:00 AM to 3:30 PM. Call (773) 238-3838.
